fields.sentence: Meren Tallowhand is the chief Keeper.

q2_gaps: modifier + agent-noun compound fused from the surface ('chief Keeper' -> chief_keeper): whether the agent-nominalization capability (Inheritance chief_keeper (can keep)) is due is undecidable as written — the fused-from-the-surface trigger and the copular-predicate trigger both fire, but the mandatory suffix test ('stripping -er must leave a verb that stands on its own') fails on the whole symbol (chief_keep), the same way it fails on the instruction set's own egg_layer example
review.notes: Fusing 'chief Keeper' as a role title, emitting the head genus and suppressing the rank-adjective modifier genus (the 'assistant secretary' case), and Member for the named individual are all exactly as specified. No capability atom is emitted; whether that is an omission turns entirely on the gap above.

fields.sentence: Meren Tallowhand tends a Cliff Path station.

review.notes: Follows the "a Northgate spokesman" proper-noun-premodifier pattern exactly (head noun typed on its own witness + opaque Possession + Name, no fusion), and (Member cliff_path path) is the licensed kind-word-inside-the-name type atom. Theme for "tends a station" rests on the "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" tie-break; a maintenance reading (clean/fix/water) would argue Patient.

fields.sentence: Meren Tallowhand is married to Joren Salt.

review.notes: 'married to' is named in the stative symmetric-predicate list, so the assert-once-plus-Symmetric-tag form and the open-class head Married are both licensed. Multi-word names are single opaque symbols with exactly one Name atom each, and no kind atom is invented.

No capability atom is owed even though the nominalization is the copular predicate: the agent-nominalization test is suffix-bound to -er/-or/-ist/-ant, which 'fisherman' fails, so it stays a plain single-lemma kind.
